LESSON: READING 4.2.2 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Months of the Year Suggested vocabulary later, before, after, sunrise, daylight,
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.2 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.2.2 Fluency, part of Months of the Year Suggested vocabulary later, before, after, sunrise, daylight, in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce sounds correctly? 2. Why should we read a story at the right speed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. select words featuring the target letter-sound combinations (/ ŋ /,/ iː/, -y, st, gl-) in a text, with peers.

2. practice reading words with the letter-sound combinations, with peers.

3. engage in timed reading 50 words per minute, observing stress and intonation.

4. read a short print (low vision) or digital text while learners with blindness read a short braille or digital text using digital device with assistive technology featuring words with the target letter-sound combinations expressively and fluently.

5. practice reading sentences aloud containing non-decodable words with target letter-sound combinations. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. select words featuring the target letter-sound combinations (/ ŋ /,/ iː/, -y, st, gl-) in a text, with peers.
2. practice reading words with the letter-sound combinations, with peers.
3. engage in timed reading 50 words per minute, observing stress and intonation.
4. read a short print (low vision) or digital text while learners with blindness read a short braille or digital text using digital device with assistive technology featuring words with the target letter-sound combinations expressively and fluently.
5. practice reading sentences aloud containing non-decodable words with target letter-sound combinations. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.2.2 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn- is developed as the learner practices reading fluently.

• Digital literacy as the learner’s ability to interact with digital devices with assistive technology is enhanced as they read digital texts.

Values:
Unity; the learner’s ability to cooperate with others is nurtured as they collaborate with peers in group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem); the learner’s esteem is nurtured when they acquire reading fluency skills.

Link to other learning areas:

Reading is linked to all other learning areas.
